subject.title: [Bug]: Cron isolated agentTurn skips delivery before dispatch when a recovered early tool error is classified as fatal

question: Should recovered exec/tool failures with evidence that the process ran become a degraded cron outcome with delivery attempted, or should they remain fatal until a narrower typed failure-phase contract exists?
rationale: The current behavior is source-reproducible, but choosing the fix changes cron execution, delivery, alerting, and retry semantics and could either lose successful reports or suppress real failures.

options.title: Add typed degraded outcome
options.body: Introduce typed process-started/failure-phase evidence and persist a degraded or warning cron outcome that allows delivery when the final assistant result is otherwise valid.

options.title: Keep fatal, improve diagnostics
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior and add explicit not-attempted/failure-phase diagnostics so users can see that delivery was skipped before dispatch.

options.title: Limit recovery to non-mutating tools
options.body: Only recover read-only or explicitly non-mutating tool failures and leave mutating or ambiguous exec failures fatal.

recommendation.title: Add typed degraded outcome
recommendation.body: Introduce typed process-started/failure-phase evidence and persist a degraded or warning cron outcome that allows delivery when the final assistant result is otherwise valid.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, commented with the current product-direction boundary, and recently maintained the affected cron code.
